subject.title: fix(heartbeat): suppress Conversation info block for synthetic heartbeat turns

question: Should the heartbeat metadata fix use the caller-owned `opts.isHeartbeat` guard, or should OpenClaw accept provider-id suppression inside the generic inbound metadata builder?
rationale: Both open PRs address the same bug, but this branch changes a broader formatter boundary while the runner already supplies a narrower heartbeat signal.

options.title: Require caller-owned suppression
options.body: Rework or choose the candidate that skips `inboundUserContext` at `runPreparedReply` for heartbeat runs and leaves `buildInboundUserContextPrefix` generic.

options.title: Accept formatter suppression
options.body: Merge the provider-id guard knowingly, owning the extra synthetic-provider policy list in the metadata helper.

options.title: Pause until one PR is canonical
options.body: Hold both open candidates until one branch is rebased, proof-positive, and selected as the landing path.

recommendation.title: Require caller-owned suppression
recommendation.body: Rework or choose the candidate that skips `inboundUserContext` at `runPreparedReply` for heartbeat runs and leaves `buildInboundUserContextPrefix` generic.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent heartbeat runner and auto-reply refactor history makes this the best available owner for the caller-boundary choice.
